title: Slow Wi-Fi in one corner of the office
symptom: Wi-Fi is fine in most of the office but very slow in one corner
user_description: The Wi-Fi is fine at the front of the office but in our corner it's painfully slow and keeps lagging.

options.why: Hugely expensive and pointless. The fault is where the signal is weak, not in the laptops.

options.text: Change the Wi-Fi password for the whole office
options.why: A password change does not affect signal strength and would disconnect everyone.

options.text: Measure signal strength and speed in that corner against other areas, check for obstacles or interference, and report the weak coverage so an access point can be moved or added
options.why: Measuring proves it is a coverage problem. Walls, metal and other equipment weaken signal, and the fix is usually repositioning or adding an access point.

options.text: Tell staff to use their phone data instead
options.why: Moves business work onto personal data and leaves the cause unsolved.

hints: Is the problem the whole network or only one place?
What can weaken a Wi-Fi signal between an access point and a corner?
Who can change where access points are placed?
real_world_tip: Walk the area with a laptop or phone and note the signal bars. A simple map of strong and weak spots makes the report convincing.
